title: Adding, Subtracting, Multiplying and Dividing Decimals
summary: Estimate and calculate with decimals: add and subtract with different numbers of decimal places, and multiply and divide decimals by whole numbers — with written methods, worked examples and practice.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Estimate, then add and subtract numbers with the same or a different number of decimal places, e.g. 14.6 + 7.85 and 20 − 6.37 (6Nf.09)
Estimate, then multiply numbers with one or two decimal places by 1-digit and 2-digit whole numbers, e.g. 6.28 × 4 and 3.6 × 27 (6Nf.10)
Estimate, then divide numbers with one or two decimal places by whole numbers, e.g. 9.72 ÷ 4 and 45.6 ÷ 12 (6Nf.11)

blocks.text: Decimals are everywhere — money, lengths, masses, times in a race. The good news: you already know how to add, subtract, multiply and divide whole numbers. With decimals you use **exactly the same methods**; you just have to keep the decimal point in the right place. Estimating first is your safety net: it tells you roughly where the point should go.
Key words

items: decimal point
العلامة العشرية — separates the whole number part from the tenths and hundredths
decimal places
الخانات العشرية — digits after the point; 3.47 has two decimal places
tenths / hundredths
أجزاء من عشرة / من مئة — 0.4 is 4 tenths, 0.07 is 7 hundredths
placeholder zero
صفر لحفظ الخانة — a 0 that fills an empty place: 5.6 = 5.60
estimate
تقدير — round the numbers to get an easy rough answer
exchange (regroup)
الاستلاف / التبديل — 1 one = 10 tenths, 1 tenth = 10 hundredths
inverse
العملية العكسية — + and − undo each other; × and ÷ undo each other
short division
القسمة المختصرة — the 'bus stop' method

blocks.text: 1. Estimate first

Round each number to something easy (usually the nearest whole number, or a number that fits a times table), then calculate in your head. Do this **before** the exact calculation and compare at the end.
2. Adding and subtracting decimals

items: Estimate.
Write the numbers in columns with the **decimal points in a straight line** (so tenths are under tenths, hundredths under hundredths).
Fill empty places with **placeholder zeros**: 14.6 → 14.60. A whole number has its point at the end: 20 → 20.00.
Add or subtract from the right, carrying or exchanging just like whole numbers.
Put the decimal point in the answer straight under the other points. Compare with your estimate.

blocks.text: For subtraction, placeholder zeros are even more important, because you need something to exchange from. 20 − 6.37 is written 20.00 − 6.37. Exchange 1 ten → 10 ones, 1 one → 10 tenths, 1 tenth → 10 hundredths, so the top number becomes 1 ten, 9 ones, 9 tenths and 10 hundredths. Then 10 − 7 = 3, 9 − 3 = 6, 9 − 6 = 3, 1 − 0 = 1: **13.63**.

A quicker **mental method** for subtracting from a whole number is **counting up** on an empty number line: jump to the next tenth, then to the next whole number, then to the target, and add the jumps.

blocks.title: Check with the inverse
blocks.text: After subtracting, add your answer to the number you took away: 13.63 + 6.37 should give 20.00. After adding, subtract one number from the total.
3. Multiplying decimals by whole numbers
**Method 1 — remove the point, multiply, put it back.** 6.28 is 628 hundredths. So 6.28 × 4 is 628 hundredths × 4 = 2512 hundredths = 25.12. In practice:

items: Ignore the point and multiply whole numbers: 628 × 4 = 2512.
The decimal had **2 decimal places**, so the answer has 2 decimal places: 25.12.
Check against the estimate: 25.12 is close to 24 ✓

blocks.text: **Method 2 — the grid method** splits both numbers by place value. It is a good way to see what is happening and works well for 2-digit multipliers.

blocks.caption: 3.6 × 27: split 27 into 20 + 7 and 3.6 into 3 + 0.6, multiply each pair, then add the four parts.

blocks.text: With **long multiplication**, multiply as whole numbers and then place the point: 36 × 27 = 36 × 7 + 36 × 20 = 252 + 720 = 972, and 3.6 has one decimal place, so 3.6 × 27 = 97.2.

blocks.title: Zeros at the end
blocks.text: 2.35 × 14 = 32.90. The zero at the end of a decimal can be dropped: 32.90 = 32.9. But for money, write two decimal places: $32.90.
4. Dividing decimals by whole numbers

Use **short division** (bus stop) exactly as for whole numbers. Put the decimal point in the answer **directly above** the point in the number you are dividing. If there is a remainder at the end, write a zero after the last digit and keep going.

blocks.caption: 8.7 ÷ 6 = 1.45. A placeholder zero (8.70) lets the division finish.

blocks.text: For a **2-digit divisor** such as 12, write out a few multiples first (12, 24, 36, 48, 60 …). 45.6 ÷ 12: 12 into 45 goes 3 times (36), remainder 9. Bring down the 6 tenths to make 96 tenths. 96 ÷ 12 = 8. So 45.6 ÷ 12 = **3.8**. Estimate: 48 ÷ 12 = 4 ✓. Check: 3.8 × 12 = 45.6 ✓

blocks.title: سر العلامة العشرية
blocks.text: في الجمع والطرح: رتّب الأرقام بحيث العلامات العشرية تيجي تحت بعض بالظبط، وكمّل الخانات الفاضية بأصفار (5.6 = 5.60 و 20 = 20.00). في الضرب: اضرب من غير العلامة، وبعدين رجّعها بنفس عدد الخانات العشرية. في القسمة: العلامة العشرية في الناتج بتطلع فوق العلامة اللي في المقسوم على طول. ودايماً قدّر الإجابة الأول علشان تعرف مكان العلامة صح.
5. Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — Work out 14.6 + 7.85 [1]
Estimate 15 + 8 = 23. Write 14.60 + 7.85 with the points lined up (see the diagram in section 2). **Answer: 22.45.** Common mistake: lining up the 6 under the 5 to get 9.31.
**Worked example 2** — Work out 20 − 6.37 [1]
Estimate 20 − 6 = 14. Either column subtraction with 20.00, or counting up: 0.03 + 0.6 + 13 = **13.63**. Check: 13.63 + 6.37 = 20 ✓
**Worked example 3** — Work out 6.28 × 4 [1]
**Worked example 4** — Work out 3.6 × 27. Show your working. [2]

Grid: 20 × 3 = 60, 7 × 3 = 21, 20 × 0.6 = 12, 7 × 0.6 = 4.2. Total 60 + 21 + 12 + 4.2 = **97.2**. Estimate 4 × 25 = 100 ✓. Mark scheme style: M1 for a complete correct method (grid or 36 × 27 = 972 seen), A1 for 97.2. Common mistake: writing 0.6 × 7 = 42 instead of 4.2 — check each part: 0.6 × 7 is 6 tenths × 7 = 42 tenths = 4.2.
**Worked example 5** — Work out 9.72 ÷ 4 [1]
**Worked example 6** — Work out 8.7 ÷ 6 [2]
Estimate 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5. 8 ÷ 6 = 1 r 2; 27 ÷ 6 = 4 r 3; write 8.70 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5. **Answer: 1.45.** Common mistake: stopping at 1.4 remainder 3 — at Stage 6 you continue with a placeholder zero.
**Worked example 7** — Pens cost $4.75 each. Karim buys 12 pens. He pays with a $100 note. How much change should he get? [2]

items: M1 for 4.75 × 12 or 57 seen; A1 for $43 (or $43.00).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Lining up the right-hand digits instead of the decimal points (3.5 + 1.25 written as 0.35 + 1.25).
Forgetting that a whole number has a hidden point: 7 − 2.85 → 7.00 − 2.85, not 2.85 − 7 or 0.7 − 2.85.
Losing or moving the point when multiplying: 5.4 × 16 = 864 ✗ — the estimate (about 80) shows the answer must be 86.4.
In division, not keeping the point directly above the point, or stopping with a remainder instead of adding a zero.
Dropping digits: 0.84 ÷ 7 = 0.12, not 1.2 or 0.012 — write the 0 in the ones place.
In money problems, writing $43.0 or 43 pence/cents confusion — use two decimal places for money ($43.00).

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: Straight calculations with an answer box on Paper 1 (no calculator) — show your working in the space, because a 2-mark question can give 1 mark for a correct method.
Complete a written method: fill the missing digits in a column addition, a grid or a short division.
Ring the best estimate or 'Tick the calculation with the largest answer' — round first.
Use a given fact: 'Use 23 × 17 = 391 to work out 2.3 × 17 or 39.1 ÷ 17.'
Spot and explain a mistake in someone's working (lined-up digits, misplaced point).

Multi-step word problems with money, litres, metres and kilograms — on Paper 2 a calculator is allowed, but you still need to choose the right operations and interpret the display (e.g. 43 means $43.00).

blocks.title: تقدير الإجابة
blocks.text: قبل ما تحسب، قرّب الأرقام: 3.6 × 27 تقريباً 4 × 25 = 100، يبقى الإجابة الصح لازم تكون قريبة من 100 (وهي 97.2) مش 972 ولا 9.72. التقدير ده هو اللي بيحميك من غلطة مكان العلامة العشرية.
Practice

blocks.title: Calculating with decimals — practice
blocks.intro: 14 questions, from easy to Checkpoint-hard. Do them without a calculator, writing your working on paper. Type only the number in the answer box.

questions.e: Line up the points and write 5.6 as 5.60: 5.60 + 3.47 = **9.07**. Estimate: 6 + 3 = 9 ✓
12.30 − 4.56: hundredths 0 − 6, exchange → 10 − 6 = 4; tenths 2 − 5, exchange → 12 − 5 = 7; ones 11 − 4 = 7; tens 0. Answer **7.74**. Check: 7.74 + 4.56 = 12.30 ✓

questions.q: Which is the best estimate for 6.9 × 31?

questions.e: Estimate: 5 × 16 = 80. Without the point: 54 × 16 = 54 × 10 + 54 × 6 = 540 + 324 = 864. One decimal place → **86.4**. Close to 80 ✓ (M1 for 864 seen or a correct grid.)

questions.q: Sami works out 3.5 + 1.25 and gets 1.60. What mistake did he make?
c: He lined up the last digits instead of the decimal points
He forgot to carry a digit
questions.e: If the last digits are lined up, 3.5 is treated as 0.35, and 0.35 + 1.25 = 1.60. With the decimal points lined up: 3.50 + 1.25 = 4.75.

questions.q: Work out the length of one side.
questions.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. 40.2 ÷ 6: 40 ÷ 6 = 6 r 4; 42 ÷ 6 = 7. **6.7 cm**. Check: 6.7 × 6 = 40.2 ✓

questions.q: Use this fact to write the answers to (i) 2.3 × 17 (ii) 39.1 ÷ 17. Explain how you know.
questions.ms: 1 mark: (i) 39.1. 1 mark: (ii) 2.3. Accept explanations such as '2.3 is 23 ÷ 10, so the answer is 391 ÷ 10' and 'division is the inverse of multiplication'. Both answers can earn the marks without an explanation if correct.
questions.e: (i) 2.3 is ten times smaller than 23, so 2.3 × 17 is ten times smaller than 391: **39.1**. (ii) Since 2.3 × 17 = 39.1, the inverse gives 39.1 ÷ 17 = **2.3**.

questions.q: Which calculation has the same answer as 0.7 × 4?

blocks.title: Remember
items: Always estimate first by rounding — it tells you where the decimal point goes.
Add and subtract: line up the decimal points; fill gaps with zeros (5.6 = 5.60, 20 = 20.00).
Multiply by a whole number: multiply without the point, then give the answer the same number of decimal places.
Divide by a whole number: short division with the answer's point straight above; add zeros to finish.
Check with the inverse operation.
